slides.texte_overlay:
lessons from history that
still apply to your life

empires fall slowly

rome didn't collapse in a day. it declined through small habits nobody noticed. your life works the same way, so the little things you repeat matter most.

the stoics were right

marcus aurelius wrote that we suffer more in imagination than in reality. most of the things you worry about tonight will never actually happen at all.

copying works

renaissance painters learned by copying the masters for years. copying people you admire isn't cheating, it's how almost every great skill has always begun.

small daily study

many great thinkers in history set aside a little time every day to learn. 5 minutes of daily learning, kept up for years, quietly turns ordinary people into brilliant ones.
slides.texte_sophia:
small daily study

great thinkers studied a little every day. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson a day, 5 minutes on a myth or a planet, and over the years it quietly makes you brilliant.

slides.texte_overlay:
plans always change

no battle plan survives first contact, as the old saying goes. make plans anyway, but hold them loosely, because the people who adapt fastest usually win.
